commit 694261cf0: _hooks_status now renders the three hook labels from hr_title = HR.title_of(HR.default_id()); default-claude output unchanged (Claude Code). Regression test test_status_label_follows_the_default_harness added to tests/test_hook_table.py.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not actually test the non-claude default-harness case and does not verify that the label is derived from `HR.default_id()`. It monkeypatches `HR.title_of` but leaves `HR.default_id` uncontrolled, then asserts `Harness<claude>`. If the default harness is something else (for example by `monkeypatch.setattr(HR, "default_id", lambda: "codex")`, or in an environment/config where `HR.default_id()` returns `codex`), the test fails or errors even though the production code would use the default harness title, so it is not a valid regression test for the stated bug. Conversely, if `hooks.py` were changed to `hr_title = HR.title_of("claude")`, the test would still pass because the patched `title_of` returns `Harness<claude>`, so the test is vacuous with respect to “follows the default harness.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_hook_table.py:202

chunk_findings.detail: The change only relabels the three hook lines; the non-Claude default-harness path still evaluates `_precompact_line(repo)` and `_pretool_line(repo)` inside the message f-string. Those lines call `CH.spec(HR.default_id(), ...)`, which the bug itself says raises `KeyError` for a non-Claude default. Given `HR.default_id() == "gemini"`, `API.hooks(repo, action="status")` still raises before returning any status message, so the named non-Claude failure mode is not fixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/hooks.py:409 `_hooks_status`

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test monkeypatches `HR.title_of` but never changes `HR.default_id()` away from `"claude"`, so it asserts `Harness<claude>` and never exercises the non-Claude default harness that `B-setup-hooks-status-claude-label` describes. chunk_findings.detail: The added regression test still does not exercise the non-Claude default-harness case that defines `B-setup-hooks-status-claude-label`. It monkeypatches `HR.title_of` but leaves `HR.default_id()` uncontrolled/ambient (normally `"claude"`), then asserts a Claude-derived label such as `Harness<claude>`. Given a non-Claude default harness, e.g. `monkeypatch.setattr(HR, "default_id", lambda: "codex")` or a config where `HR.default_id()` returns `"codex"`, the production code would now use the Codex label and the new no-hook branches, but this test would fail because it expects the Claude label. Conversely, if `_hooks_status` were implemented as `HR.title_of("claude")` while `HR.default_id()` remained `"claude"`, the test would still pass, so it does not prove that the label follows `HR.default_id()` and does not cover the new `_hook_spec(...) is None` behavior for missing non-Claude hooks.

A still-hardcoded implementation using `HR.title_of("claude")` would pass, and the non-Claude default-harness path from B-setup-hooks-status-claude-label—including the former `KeyError` path—is never tested. Previous findings 1 and 3 still hold and are not answered by the hooks.py diff.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_hook_table.py:202 test_status_label_follows_the_default_harness

chunk_findings.detail: The new test sets `HR.default_id` to `"gemini"` and then asserts the status message contains `"Gemini CLI PreCompact hook"` and `"Gemini CLI PreToolUse hook"`. Per the bug itself, those hook kinds exist only in the Claude hook spec—that is exactly why `_precompact_line`/`_pretool_line` raise `KeyError` for a non-Claude default, and the test's own docstring says the non-Claude harness lacks those hooks. A correct fix to the non-Claude status path would omit hook kinds the default harness does not have; in that correct implementation these assertions fail. The test therefore forces the code to print PreCompact/Pretool lines for a harness that has none, contradicting the bug it is meant to guard.
